why: Both engineers found the same real hooks (create_client, the four inline reviewer clients, the ICLR benchmark's duplicate dispatch, aider's LiteLLM path) and the same blocking trade-off (seed=0 on every OpenAI call), and both are honest about the n>1 ensemble, the non-catalog model pins, Bedrock/Vertex, and the pre-existing anthropic-1.13 temperature break. B edges ahead on substance: its seed policy is scoped to the whole llm.py label space rather than one function, so the n=1 batch path — the ICLR benchmark's actual default — routes too; it caught that the codemod's relative-then-bare import resolves to neither from a top-level script and would have silently bound the no-op wrapper; it measured Claude prefix caching (-67%) on the review ensemble's real ~10k-token prompt; and it is right that none of the app's current pins have a Flex tier, which correctly makes the model-pin move the gate for everything else.
A_best: Reached Router leverage B only proposed: the reviewer on gpt-5.4-mini at Flex measured at 82% less per call, offered as a branch mutually exclusive with the conservative same-family gpt-4o move, so the CTO picks a price point rather than a plumbing detail — plus a crisp, principled refusal of fallbacks and provider_timeout (silent model substitution is a provenance decision in a paper-publishing pipeline; a timeout turns a slow call into an abandoned idea).
B_best: The depth is in the corrections and the census: it fixed an import that would have silently disabled routing in three entry points, deleted three byte-identical copies of the runtime down to one, enumerated 13-of-41 catalog resolution over AVAILABLE_LLMS to show that a default-model run routes nothing from llm.py, and added the operational half nobody else did — a capped per-deployment Router key, with the observation that caps are enforced after usage is recorded so parallel aider loops can overshoot, and that the per-idea try/except degrades a resulting 401 to one lost idea.
A_worst: The policy glob is pinned to get_response_from_llm, so get_batch_responses_from_llm stays unrouted even at n=1 — which is the ICLR benchmark's default and a path A itself claims to have moved; and it repeats the codemod's relative-then-bare import in llm.py without noticing that pattern's silent-no-op failure mode.
B_worst: Half the system-level work is proposal rather than branch — most consequentially it never touches Flex, deferring the single largest price lever behind the model-pin decision instead of building and measuring one concrete Flex option the way A did, and its one built reviewer branch (route-reviewer-model) buys coverage without a measured saving.
